raw_response:
Six existing designs are useful for this problem. The first five have versioned or dated evidence before the 2014-07-15 cutoff; the D evidence is a live page with unknown historical availability.

1. **C++11/N3337 attributes on statements and declarations.** [Statement grammar](https://timsong-cpp.github.io/cppwp/n3337/stmt.stmt) and [declaration grammar](https://timsong-cpp.github.io/cppwp/n3337/dcl.dcl) show attributes attached directly to blocks and local declarations. This is a useful syntax model for precise lint or audit metadata. Individual attributes still need target and semantic rules; grammar alone does not provide conditional compilation. Evidence: N3337, dated 2012-01-16.

2. **Nimrod 0.9.4 local pragmas, push/pop regions, and when statements.** The [versioned manual](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nim-lang/Nim/v0.9.4/doc/manual.txt) demonstrates per-variable pragmas, temporary compiler settings, and inline compile-time branches. These preserve access to surrounding state. Push/pop restoration is explicit, each pragma has allowed targets, and the [2014-04-21 release](https://nim-lang.org/blog/2014/04/21/version-094-released.html) was labeled beta quality.

3. **GCC diagnostic push/pop.** The [GCC 4.7.0 manual](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-4.7.0/gcc.pdf), section 6.57.10, demonstrates a warning exception around selected source lines with policy restored afterward. This supplies an implementation model for narrow lint allowances. It uses source-location state and explicit restoration, not automatic block boundaries; only supported warnings are controllable. A [2010 implementation patch](https://gcc.gnu.org/pipermail/gcc-patches/2010-June/286132.html) documents the underlying history mechanism.

4. **Java local-variable @SuppressWarnings.** The [Java SE 6 API](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/api/java/lang/SuppressWarnings.html) permits source-retained warning annotations on local declarations and combines their suppressions with enclosing annotations. This helps define declaration-level lint scope. It does not cover arbitrary blocks or conditional compilation. The API identifies the feature as available since Java 1.5.

5. **C# unsafe and checked/unchecked block contexts.** [ECMA-334, fourth edition, June 2006](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-334_4th_edition_june_2006.pdf), sections 27.1 and 15.11, supplies precedents for bounded permissions and checking policies around inline blocks. This supports a small-block annotation design without extracting a function. These built-in contexts neither provide arbitrary metadata nor prove the marked code safe.

6. **D conditional statements and declarations.** The [conditional-compilation specification](https://dlang.org/spec/version.html) supports version, debug, and static-if selection of inline code without a new scope. This addresses function duplication and manual local-state transfer. Excluded branches must remain syntactically valid, and conditional braces do not create scope. This is conditional-compilation machinery, not general audit metadata. Its availability at the cutoff is unverified because only the live specification was opened.

These are transfer candidates, not claims that any mechanism has been deployed or validated for this Rust design. Native unauthenticated grep.app code search succeeded; no code-through-web fallback was required.
